questions.question: When you say the panel 'walked' the screens, does that mean it actually rendered and interacted with the live UI, or just reasoned over code and a static viewport?
questions.why: The panel said DONE on a phone that was unusable, so the mechanics of how it 'walks' a screen are the whole crux of the failure.

questions.question: Is '9 seconds, simulated' a usability number at all, or is it just an agent describing its own read of the screen?
questions.why: The speaker flags it himself as simulated, not human, which is exactly the kind of AI-user-research number the persona distrusts.

questions.question: Who actually turns a persona's NOT verdict into a design change, and can that person decline what the persona is asking for?
questions.why: The talk never says whether a human designer sits between the panel's verdict and what ships.

questions.question: Are the four persona briefs built from real usability research, or are they demographics like '22, phone-only' dressed up as jobs?
questions.why: Dez's brief is described in one line on the slide, with no mention of where it came from.

questions.question: After the panel missed the fixed-viewport failure, did you change how the panel walks screens, or just add the human phone check on top?
questions.why: The stated fix was 'another panel pass,' which sounds like re-running the same flawed method rather than fixing the gate itself.

questions.question: What did the flapping actually look like to someone trying to use the scout, and did you watch a real person react to it before calling it fixed?
questions.why: Jitter is framed entirely through drop-rate metrics, never through what a confused user on a real stream experienced.

questions.question: What specifically changed on the review screen that cut your labeling verdict from three minutes to twenty seconds, and did anyone other than you time it?
questions.why: The 20-30 second number is the speaker's own stopwatch on himself, with no second labeler cited.

questions.question: Since one panel already returned a false DONE on a real device, how many other screens have you not yet re-checked by hand?
questions.why: If the fixed-viewport bug slipped through once, other undetected false-DONE verdicts seem likely across the rest of the product.

questions.question: Do the persona briefs ever get revised based on what real users actually do, or do they stay fixed once written?
questions.why: A static persona brief that never absorbs real research is exactly what breeds false confidence at the done gate.

questions.question: For the live demo, was the card that held actually held long enough for a hand to tap it, or just long enough to look stable on stage?
questions.why: The demo script explicitly stages the hold and tells him to leave it alone for a few seconds, which reads as a performance choice, not evidence of usability.
